findings.summary: the --accept-edits validation chain never consults dry_run or local, so `crew review --plan X --accept-edits "<reason>" --dry-run` passes every check and reaches the write branch at reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2750, which persists the accepted-edits entry and git-commits the review record; --dry-run is documented as a preview and the sibling --answer branch in the same function refuses the combination outright (`elif dry_run or local: detail = "--dry-run and --local apply only to review dispatch"`), so the new mutating option is the one path of this verb that writes under a flag promising it will not. Reproduced at the reviewed head 0601bc4fc2 with the node's own fixture: invoking the verb with --accept-edits and --dry-run writes ACCEPTED_EDITS_KEY into the stored review (probe-dry-run.log, 1 failed, EXIT=1).

the acceptance selects over the incomplete reviews *filtered out*, so when the newest stored review is marked incomplete the entry lands silently on an older review instead of the plan section's "newest stored review"; and because nothing incomplete is ever passed to it, accept_edits' own incomplete refusal (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2405) is unreachable from the verb, so the case that refusal guards is untested end to end.

review_scope now prints an `- accepted-edits [...]` line for each acceptance, which is half of the plan section's deliverable ("the record ... is listed with the review's answers, so an accepted edit is never silent"), and no test asserts it: all seven added cases read coverage and the stored entry, so this listing could be deleted with no red test.

the manifest's artifacts line states that ruff check and ruff format --check are clean on the three staged paths, but no ruff log is among its test_logs, so the done-when's third measure can only be quoted from the worker's account; I re-ran both at the reviewed head and they hold (All checks passed! on the three paths, 3 files already formatted), so the claim is true and only the artefact is missing.
